_doc: The Crown's Purse (src/systems/fiscal.js, src/world/crownBooks.js). Each realm keeps real books: taxes come out of its towns' purses (economy.gold, where their production and trade income is credited) and wages and upkeep go back into them, so taxation moves gold, never makes it. Revenue lines: land tax (the peasants' earnings x the harvest, plus part of the town's production gold), poll or hearth tax (taxable heads: peasants, artisans, merchants; clergy and nobles exempt), excise (the artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade income), customs (systems/tradePolicy.js and the crown's tolls), the demesne (the crown's own estates: a share of production gold) and monopolies, seigniorage (world/moneySupply.js), tax farms sold, the extraordinary levy, offices and crown land sold. Expense lines: army wages (field pay at war), court and administration, roads and works (world/transport.js, systems/publicWorks.js), debt service (systems/finance.js), the famine dole and granaries, the ruler's purse (systems/throne.js). Everything else that moved the treasury lands under 'other'. Set enabled false to fall back to the old income (the growth of the towns' gold). Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'The Crown's Purse'.
_levels: Tax levels: each multiplies the base rates. NPC crowns pick one level for all three taxes; a ruler sets each tax apart in the Treasury panel.

light.label: Light
light.blurb: The people prosper and stay; the chests fill slowly.

heavy.label: Heavy
heavy.blurb: The chests fill; the realm grumbles and the poor drift away.

crushing.label: Crushing
crushing.blurb: Every last penny: unrest, flight, tax revolts.

_rates: Base rates at the standard level: land (share of the peasants' earnings and of landProd x the town's production gold), poll (gold per taxable head a day), excise (share of the artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade income).
_sales: rates.sales: the land tax's share of the coin a town took for the goods it sold to other towns (economy.fySales, world/settlementMarket.js flows and the caravans), x the land tax's level; rates.hoard: a day's share of the coin a town holds past hoardReserve a head (the assessors find what the town sits on), x the land tax's level. 2026-11, when the towns' coin became real: the countryside sells the capitals their food, and the crown's tax on those sales is what brings the coin back to the capital (in the soldiers' and clerks' pay).
_collectEvery: The collectors come round each town once every collectEvery days (staggered by town) and take every day's dues since.
_fallback: Earnings per head a day for a town whose labour record is not set up yet.
_demesne: The crown's own estates: `share` of the towns' production gold (the capital's counts `capital` times). Selling crown land in a crisis gives up `crisis.land.share` of what is left for `crisis.land.days` of its yield; it never falls below `min`.
_army: Wages: pay a day per soldier (x warPay while at war, x the realm's upkeep bonuses and military-spending events), bounty per new recruit. Pay levels for a ruler (NPC crowns pay full, half when broke): mult on the wages, cap on the army the realm keeps, stability. Unpaid soldiers desert after desert.afterDays: the army the realm can keep falls capPerDay a day (never below capMin) until they are paid.

army._spendWeights: Where the army's wages are spent (systems/fiscal.js _spendBack): the towns the collectors visited, by their people x this weight for their kind (the capital's garrison and the towns' quarter more men than the villages). 2026-11: added when the towns' coin became real; by people alone the villages took the soldiers' pay and the capitals, which buy the villages' food, ran dry.

half.label: Half pay
half.blurb: Cheap, and the men drift home.

generous.label: Generous
generous.blurb: Loyal regiments, and more men take the shilling.

_court: Court and administration a day: base + perTown x towns + perHead x people, x the court level. A frugal court breeds corruption (corruption a day), a lavish one is loved.

frugal.label: Frugal
frugal.blurb: Fewer clerks, and those who stay take their own cut.

_corruption: 0-1. Unpaid officials raise it unpaidGain a day; it decays `decay` a day while they are paid. It leaks `leak` x corruption of the taxes before they reach the treasury, and adds to the people's burden. Selling offices adds officesSale.
_burden: The burden the people feel, on the labour model's scale (base 0.15 = the customary dues; world/townLabour.js welfare falls by (burden - 0.15) x taxWeight per stratum): base x the realm's tax index (land, poll and excise levels weighted), + farmPerSqueeze x (a farmer's squeeze - 1), + corruption x `corruption`.
_stability: Stability target term 'Taxes & pay': -(tax index - 1) x perLevel, -arrearsPerDay a day the soldiers and officials go unpaid (at most arrearsCap), -corruption x `corruption`, plus the pay and court levels' own.
_npc: NPC crowns review their taxes every `every` days (staggered): from the standard level, + bias by personality, + 1 at war, + 1 below reserveLow days of spending in the chests (+2 below lowDays), - 1 above reserveHigh (-2 above highDays), + 1 with soldiers unpaid, - 1 when stability is under unrestAt or a tax revolt broke out in the last revoltDays; they move one step a review. Below halfPayDays of spending with soldiers unpaid they go to half pay. The realm the player rules is reviewed on the same days by its treasurers (systems/fiscal.js _review): no personality bias, never above ruledMaxTax nor into a lavish court on their own, and only the levers (taxes, court, army pay) the ruler has not set by hand in the Treasury; each change is told to the ruler. 2026-11: added when a crowned player who left the books alone saw the chests run dry and the realm sink into arrears, corruption and unrest within a few years, while the same realm under the AI kept a reserve.
_coin: Taxes come out of the towns' purses into the crown's chests and the wages go back into them; the money supply (world/moneySupply.js) counts the purses, so this moves the realm's coin in circulation by itself (booked daily as the 'fisc' flow). No tunables left here.
_farms: Tax farming. A crown short of money (below needDays of spending, deficitWeeks weeks in deficit, at war below warDays, or with its soldiers unpaid) auctions, at most once every `cooldown` days, the taxes of one town (not its capital; at most maxShare of its towns) for term days: the lot's estimate is the town's recent crown taxes x term; a banking house bids discount (a hash in the range) of it, the player may outbid by `outbid`; the lot closes after `close` days. The farmer collects the town's taxes x squeeze (less collectCost) in place of the crown. Player squeeze levels: mult, reputation lost in the realm a day, the town's happiness a day. A house squeezes `bankSqueeze`.

gentle.label: Gentle
gentle.blurb: Collect what is owed and no more.

harsh.label: Harsh
harsh.blurb: Bailiffs and distraint. Hated, and rich.

_revolts: Tax revolts, weekly per town (a hash roll, no RNG): pressure = (burden - burdenAt) x perBurden + (welfareAt - the peasants' welfare) x perWelfare + farmed (if farmed), each at least 0; chance = min(max, pressure x chance). A revolt withholds the town's taxes for `days`, costs it `happiness`, the realm `stability`, and drives a tax farmer's men out.
_crisis: Ways out of a fiscal crisis besides borrowing, the levy, debasement and default (systems/finance.js chooses): selling offices raises `offices.days` of revenue (corruption + corruption.officesSale); selling crown land raises `land.days` of the yield of `land.share` of the demesne.
_explain: What the Treasury panel (src/ui/actionMenu/treasury.js, via src/ui/actionMenu/taxGuide.js) tells the player each tax, level and budget line is. {pct:path} prints a number of this file as a percent, {num:path} as it stands, {c100:path} times 100 (a sum per hundred), {x:path} as a multiplier: the prose follows the tuning. Per-level effects (revenue x, burden and stability) are computed from levels/burden/stability, not written here. Keep each line to what the code reads.

explain.intro: Every coin the crown takes comes out of its towns' purses (the coin their people hold), and its wages go back into them. Collectors call on each town every {num:collectEvery} days and take every day's dues since; a town whose purse is empty pays only what it has, and a town in revolt pays nothing for {num:revolts.days} days.
explain.collection: Every tax is then × the realm's collection (the steward, stability, blockades, events) and less {pct:corruption.leak} × corruption kept by the officials.

land.name: Land tax
land.who: The countryside and the town's trade: the peasants who work the land, and the town as a whole for what it makes and sells away.
land.on: The peasants' earnings (swelled or cut by the harvest), the town's production, the coin it took for goods sold to other towns, and the coin it sits on.
land.how: {pct:rates.land} of the peasants' earnings × the harvest (×0.5 to ×1.5), + {pct:rates.land} of {pct:rates.landProd} of the town's production gold, + {pct:rates.sales} of the coin from goods sold to other towns, + {pct:rates.hoard} a day of the coin it holds past {num:rates.hoardReserve}g a head. All × the land tax's level.
land.weight: It is {pct:burden.weights.land} of the realm's tax index: a step on the land tax moves the burden and stability twice as far as a step on the hearth tax or the excise.

poll.name: Hearth tax
poll.who: Every working head: peasants and artisans count once, merchants {x:pollWeights.merchants}; clergy and nobles are exempt.
poll.on: Heads, not earnings: a poor town pays as much per person as a rich one.
poll.how: {c100:rates.poll}g a day for every 100 taxable heads, × the hearth tax's level.
poll.weight: It is {pct:burden.weights.poll} of the realm's tax index.

excise.name: Excise
excise.on: The artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade income.
excise.how: {pct:rates.excise} of the artisans' earnings + {pct:rates.excise} of the town's trade income, × the excise's level.
excise.weight: It is {pct:burden.weights.excise} of the realm's tax index.

explain.levels: Each level multiplies that tax's take: 🍃 Light {x:levels.light.mult}, ⚖️ Standard {x:levels.standard.mult}, 💰 Heavy {x:levels.heavy.mult}, ⛓️ Crushing {x:levels.crushing.mult}. NPC crowns set all three to one level; a ruler sets each apart.
raise: Revenue: that tax's take × the level (paid only from what the towns' purses hold).
The people's burden rises (base {pct:burden.base} × the tax index). Every class's welfare falls by (burden − 15%) × its weight, so people drift along the trade roads to towns that treat them better.

Tax revolts: above a burden of {pct:revolts.burdenAt} (or where the peasants are hard-pressed), each town risks a revolt each week (at most {pct:revolts.max}): no taxes for {num:revolts.days} days, −{num:revolts.happiness} happiness there, −{num:revolts.stability} stability.
Stability: the realm's target falls {num:stability.perLevel} for each whole step the tax index stands above Standard (and rises as much below it).
Coin: taxes take real coin out of the towns' purses into the chests, and wages put it back. The coin in the chests moves no prices until it is spent.
explain.lower: Lowering does the reverse: less gold, a lighter burden (people stay and settlers come), fewer revolts, a steadier realm. Light taxes can leave the army unpaid: soldiers unpaid more than {num:army.desert.afterDays} days desert.
explain.army: Army wages: {num:army.pay}g a day per soldier (×{num:army.warPay} at war, × the realm's upkeep bonuses), + {num:army.bounty}g for each new recruit, × the pay level. Paid before the court. Soldiers spend it where they are quartered.
explain.court: Court & administration: {num:court.base}g + {num:court.perTown}g a town + {num:court.perHead}g a head, a day, × the court level. The clerks spend it in the capital.

terms.burden: The people's burden: what the taxes weigh on them ({pct:burden.base} is the customary due). Raised by the tax levels, a tax farmer's squeeze and corruption.
terms.stability: The 'Taxes & pay' part of the realm's stability: the tax levels, unpaid days (up to −{num:stability.arrearsCap}), corruption (−{num:stability.corruption} at 100%), and the army-pay and court levels.
terms.corruption: The share of officials on the take: {pct:corruption.leak} of it leaks out of the taxes. It grows while the clerks go unpaid, under a frugal court and when offices are sold, and fades while they are paid.
terms.demesne: The crown's own estates: their share of the land's production gold (the capital's counts {x:demesne.capital}). Selling crown land shrinks it for good.
terms.reserve: Days in hand: how many days of spending the chests would cover.

lines.land: The land tax: on the peasants' earnings (by the harvest), the town's production and its sales to other towns.
lines.poll: The hearth tax: so much a working head (merchants more, clergy and nobles exempt).
lines.excise: The excise: on the artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade.
lines.customs: Tariffs on goods crossing the border, and the crown's road, bridge and canal tolls.
lines.demesne: The crown's own estates (a share of the land's gold) and its monopolies (licences, the post).
lines.seigniorage: The mint's profit on striking and re-striking the realm's coin.
lines.farms: Lump sums paid by tax farmers who bought the right to collect a town's taxes.
lines.levy: An extraordinary levy: an extra share on every tax while it runs (a crown deep in debt), and forced gifts from its subjects.
lines.sales: One-off sales: offices, crown land, licences and petitions, and surplus arms sold off.
lines.escheat: What an heirless estate leaves the crown once its banks and creditors are paid (player/estateSettlement.js).
lines.heriot: Death duties: the share of a vassal's purse the crown takes when an heir inherits (systems/inheritance.js).
lines.army: Soldiers' daily pay and recruits' bounties, the fleet's upkeep, field costs, and wages the crown pays its commissioned officers (you, when you serve).
lines.arms: Weapons, shields, helms, harness and arrows the crown buys from its towns' markets to arm its soldiers.
lines.court: The household, officers and clerks (by the realm's size), and the upkeep of royal edicts.
lines.guard: The household guard the crown keeps riding with its lords: each company's wage, paid daily from the treasury.
lines.works: Building and keeping up roads, bridges, canals and other public works.
lines.debt: Interest and repayments on the crown's loans from the banking houses.
lines.dole: Famine relief: grain bought for the hungry and to stock the granaries.
lines.purse: The ruler's own cut of the crown's revenue (the royal levy: your gold, if you rule).
lines.loans: Gold borrowed from the banking houses (not income: it must be paid back).
lines.debase: Gold made by debasing the coin (prices rise after).
lines.other: Everything else that moved the treasury (events, tribute, temples, licences): the books always balance.

_smoothing: Daily smoothing of the books' average revenue and spending (the Finance tick's income and the reserve).
